title.en: Rus': from Rurik to Ivan III

description.en: Six centuries of Russian history: the Varangians, Kiev and Christianisation, the break-up into principalities, Horde rule, the rise of Moscow and Ivan III's united state.

text.en: According to the Primary Chronicle, Slavic and Finnic tribes invited the Varangian Rurik to rule over them. Chronicle tradition dates the beginning of Rus' and of the Rurikid dynasty, which ruled for over seven centuries, to this event.

According to the Primary Chronicle, Prince Oleg of Novgorod killed Kiev's rulers Askold and Dir and made the city his capital. The union of Novgorod and Kiev is traditionally seen as the founding of the Kievan Rus' state.

Grand Prince Vladimir of Kiev adopted Byzantine Christianity and had the people of Kiev baptised in the Dnieper. The conversion tied Rus' to the Orthodox world of Byzantium and shaped its culture, literacy and statehood for centuries.
On 19 October 1097 the princes of Rus' met at Liubech to end their feuds. They proclaimed that 'each shall keep his patrimony', entrenching the division of Rus' into hereditary principalities.

After a popular uprising in 1113, the people of Kiev invited Vladimir Monomakh to the throne. He issued a statute curbing usury and briefly restored the unity of Rus', which broke apart after the death of his son Mstislav.
In 1136 Novgorod expelled Prince Vsevolod and began choosing for itself whom to invite as prince. Real power passed to the veche assembly, the posadnik and the archbishop.

Under the year 1147 the Hypatian Chronicle records Prince Yuri Dolgoruky of Suzdal inviting his ally Sviatoslav Olgovich to meet him at Moskov. It is the first chronicle mention of the future capital of Russia.
The army of Batu Khan sacked Ryazan, Vladimir and many other cities, and in 1240 Kiev. The Russian principalities fell under the overlordship of the Golden Horde for nearly two and a half centuries.
In December 1240 Batu's army took Kiev after a siege. The last defenders sheltered in the Church of the Tithes, which collapsed.

Forces led by Prince Alexander Nevsky defeated the knights of the Livonian Order on the frozen Lake Peipus. The victory checked the Order's eastward advance into the lands of Novgorod and Pskov and became an emblem of Russian military history.

title.en: Ivan Kalita becomes Prince of Moscow

text.en: In 1325 Ivan Kalita became Prince of Moscow, and Metropolitan Peter moved his seat to the city. Gaining the Horde's patent for the grand princely title and the right to collect tribute, Ivan I laid the basis of Moscow's rise.

Forces of the Russian principalities led by Grand Prince Dmitry of Moscow defeated the army of the Horde warlord Mamai. The victory raised Moscow's standing as the centre for uniting the Russian lands and earned Dmitry the name Donskoy.
In January 1478 Novgorod surrendered to Ivan III. Its veche assembly was abolished and the veche bell taken to Moscow.

title.en: Great Stand on the Ugra River

text.en: The armies of Grand Prince Ivan III and Khan Akhmat of the Great Horde faced each other across the Ugra River for weeks until Akhmat withdrew without battle. The event traditionally marks the end of the Tatar yoke over Russia.

source: Steps assembled from the event records included in this atlas.
